HotLoop reads and controls Shelly devices of every generation directly, finds ONVIF cameras and serves their streams, snapshots and pan, tilt and zoom, talks to Arduinos over Firmata, and sends an OPC UA password of any length the way the specification asks. A slow link no longer keeps an edge node on its disk, and `--version` names the commit an image was built from. A default install of HotLoop Edge starts. Built for amd64 only; the multi-arch build follows as the next release.

## What changed

- **Shelly, any generation.** Gen2 and later over RPC with a live websocket, so a change and a button press arrive the moment they happen, and Gen1 over its own HTTP interface. A button press is filed in the logbook under the device. See SHELLY.md.
- **ONVIF cameras.** Find cameras on the network (WS-Discovery), read each one's device information, every media profile's stream and snapshot address (Media and Media2), pan, tilt and zoom, and the camera's own events as tags and logbook lines. A profile's current picture is one route away. See ONVIF.md.
- **Arduinos over Firmata.** USB serial or TCP, with digital and analog pins, PWM, servos and I2C devices as tags. See FIRMATA.md.
- **OPC UA passwords of any length.** Passwords over 64 bytes now go over OPC UA the way the specification asks (RsaEncryptedSecret, part 4, 7.40.4), from the client and to the server, and older servers still sign in. Proven against the OPC Foundation's own stack. See [the OPC UA server](/edge/opc-ua-server/).
- **A slow link no longer pins the node to its disk.** The pass that takes the last of the disk now sends what comes in behind it from memory, so a forward queue behind a slow link empties and the node leaves the disk instead of fsyncing on every poll.
- **`--version` names the commit.** Every image says the commit it was built from as well as its version.
- **A CODESYS screen beside its WebVisu.** The import of a CODESYS visualization is run against a real WebVisu, driven by the same PLC variables, and the two are compared in a browser.
- **The docs/legacy roadmap line is ticked.**
- **A default install of HotLoop Edge starts.** The pod no longer reads the Gotify token, the Discord webhook URL or the Discord bot token from a Secret that does not exist: each is sent only when its credential is set, and the chart check fails any reference to that Secret the render does not make. A chart with a destination set, or an existing Secret named, renders as before.
- **The Ignition lab, in both directions.** HotLoop's Ignition proof now runs the other way too, a routed multicast UADP proof joins it, and the biggest report is measured. See [Scheduled reports](/gateway/reports/).
- **Tests wait for what they are waiting for.** The phone app's warm-up waits for a signed-in page, and the energy form fills its fields in one step.

## Migrations

None.

## API changes

Two routes, both new. `POST /api/onvif/discover` (`devices.write`) probes the network for ONVIF cameras and adds nothing. `GET /api/onvif/{id}/profiles/{profile}/snapshot` (`devices.read`) returns a camera profile's current JPEG. No existing route changed. See [the HTTP API](/iot/api/).

## Upgrading from 4.24.0

A plain `helm upgrade`. No migration and no new secret.

## What is not proven

- Shelly, ONVIF and Firmata ran against recordings of real devices, ONVIF's own generated stack and the Arduino project's own StandardFirmata on a simulated Uno. No physical Shelly, camera or Arduino has been on the bench yet.
- The WebVisu side-by-side runs in testing against a CODESYS Control for Linux SL 4.22.0.0 runtime.
